discovery: Invention and realization of the optical lattice clock

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Katori conceived the optical lattice clock (2001-2003), proposing that neutral atoms be trapped in an optical lattice tuned to a 'magic wavelength' at which light shifts of both clock levels cancel. This lets many atoms be interrogated at once, free of Doppler and recoil shifts, without perturbing the clock transition. Katori realized the first strontium lattice clocks. Jun Ye pushed the concept to its ultimate performance: ultrastable lasers, control of atomic interactions in degenerate Fermi gases, and systematic uncertainties and stabilities at the 10^-18 to 10^-19 level. Lattice clocks with Sr and Yb now surpass the cesium standard by more than two orders of magnitude and are driving the redefinition of the SI second. They have enabled relativistic geodesy at centimetre height resolution, gravitational redshift measured across a millimetre-scale atomic sample, and new searches for dark matter and variation of fundamental constants. Together they opened a whole new platform for precision physics.
